cases.question: Two separate experiments in the backbone findings each produced a result where a loss/optimization metric looked healthy but contradicted the behavioral-quality signal. Name the two experiments and give the specific numeric contradiction in each.
cases.reference_answer: The five-epoch overfit probe showed the best training loss was the worst generalizer: validation loss bottomed at 1.496 at epoch 2 but rose to 1.557 by epoch 5 while training loss fell to 1.32. The DPO run showed the same lesson one optimization stage later: training loss decreased and reward accuracy reached 1.0, yet only the behavioral evaluation blocked shipping, so the deployed model remained SFT rank 16.

required_claims.text: The 5-epoch overfit probe showed val loss bottomed at 1.496 at epoch 2 and rose to 1.557 by epoch 5 while train loss fell to 1.32 — the best train loss was the worst generalizer.
The DPO chain of gates showed train loss decreased and reward accuracy reached 1.0 but only behavioral eval blocked shipping; the deployed model remained SFT r16.

cases.question: The model-gate workflow has produced two real promotion PRs with different outcomes. For each PR, state the gate exit code on the first run, the reason given, and what happened next — then state the Argo CD Application setting that guarantees the merge actually reaches the cluster.
cases.reference_answer: PR #1 (Hermes-4 → Hermes-3 fallback) returned NEEDS_REVIEW on a peak-hour NextBit latency flag (environmental); a human override was documented on the PR, it was merged, GitOps-deployed, and verified serving. PR #2 (self-hosted Ollama qwen2.5:0.5b as rp-selfhosted) was first REJECTED because the gate itself exposed CI-topology drift; the topology issue was fixed, the rerun returned PROMOTE, and it was deployed. The Argo CD Application at apps/gateway.yaml is configured with automated sync plus selfHeal plus prune, so a merge to master is reconciled onto the cluster.

required_claims.text: PR #1 (Hermes-4 → Hermes-3 fallback) returned NEEDS_REVIEW on a peak-hour NextBit latency flag; human override documented, merged, GitOps-deployed, verified serving.
PR #2 (self-hosted Ollama qwen2.5:0.5b as rp-selfhosted) first run REJECTED on CI-topology drift the gate exposed; fixed, PROMOTE, deployed.

cases.question: The backbone dataset generation and the backbone pushy-user-resistance evaluation both run through the gateway's OpenRouter route, yet they deliberately adopt opposite fallback policies. What does each use, and why is the divergence principled rather than accidental?
cases.reference_answer: The dataset generation job is scripted through the gateway with a budget-capped virtual key whose spend is visible in Grafana; per-key spend enforcement comes from Postgres-backed virtual keys via /key/generate with hard max_budget caps, giving every key its own spend ledger. The pushy-user-resistance evaluation instead runs in the model lab on direct OpenRouter with NO fallback, because silent model swapping would poison the blind base-versus-fine-tune ratings the lab exists to produce. The divergence is principled: the gateway is a product/availability concern (failover keeps users served), while the lab is a measurement concern where any silent swap contaminates the very quantity being rated.

required_claims.text: Dataset generation uses the gateway with a budget-capped virtual key, spend visible in Grafana; per-key enforcement is Postgres-backed virtual keys via /key/generate with hard max_budget caps, each key has its own spend ledger.
The model lab stays on direct OpenRouter with NO fallback because silent model swapping would poison blind ratings; the gateway is a product concern, not a lab concern.

notes: AI-authored proposal only; no human review occurred.
Requires exact-source review by a model family other than GLM.

cases.question: Counting every RP model the gateway can route to, how many distinct independent infrastructures back the RP path, and what in-cluster addition was merged later as a fourth leg? Give each model's host/precision and explain why same-model host failover is not the mechanism providing diversity.
cases.reference_answer: The gateway's RP path is backed by three independent infrastructures because every checked RP-tuned 70B is single-host on OpenRouter — rp-primary is Euryale on NextBit at bf16, rp-fallback is Hermes-4 70B on Nebius at fp8, and Hermes-3 on DeepInfra at fp8. Same-model host failover does not exist for this class, so the model-level fallback chain itself is the host diversity (3 models = 3 independent infrastructures). A fourth leg was later added: rp-selfhosted, an in-cluster Ollama qwen2.5:0.5b model running on CPU, merged via gate PR #2 after an initial rejection on CI-topology drift was fixed.

required_claims.text: Every RP-tuned 70B is single-host on OpenRouter: Euryale=NextBit bf16, Hermes-4=Nebius fp8, Hermes-3=DeepInfra fp8. Same-model host failover doesn't exist; the model-level fallback chain IS the host diversity (3 models = 3 independent infrastructures).
rp-primary is Euryale 70B with automatic fallback to rp-fallback Hermes-4 70B after retries are exhausted.
rp-selfhosted is an in-cluster Ollama qwen2.5:0.5b on CPU, merged via gate PR #2 (first run REJECTED on CI-topology drift; fixed, PROMOTE, deployed).
